simple.meaning: בָּצַר (bâtsar) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to gather grapes ; also to be isolated (i.e. inaccessible by height or fortification).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 38 times across Genesis, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, Joshua, and 14 more, beginning at Genesis 11:6. Its contexts include family, family line, land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בָּצַר (H1219).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: בָּצַר (bâtsar) / H1219 is traced through Genesis 11:6, Leviticus 25:5, Leviticus 25:11, Numbers 13:28 as a generated source-based concept entry.

timeline.evidenceText: Yahweh said, “Behold, they are one people, and they all have one language, and this is what they begin to do. Now nothing will be withheld from them, which they intend to do.
What grows of itself in your harvest you shall not reap, and you shall not gather the grapes of your undressed vine. It shall be a year of solemn rest for the land.
That fiftieth year shall be a jubilee to you. In it you shall not sow, neither reap that which grows of itself, nor gather from the undressed vines.
However, the people who dwell in the land are strong, and the cities are fortified and very large. Moreover, we saw the children of Anak there.

Where are we going up? Our brothers have made our heart melt, saying, ‘The people are greater and taller than we. The cities are great and fortified up to the sky. Moreover we have seen the sons of the Anakim there!’ ”
All these were cities fortified with high walls, gates, and bars, in addition to a great many villages without walls.
Hear, Israel! You are to pass over the Jordan today, to go in to dispossess nations greater and mightier than yourself, cities great and fortified up to the sky,
When you harvest your vineyard, you shall not glean it after yourselves. It shall be for the foreigner, for the fatherless, and for the widow.

They will besiege you in all your gates until your high and fortified walls in which you trusted come down throughout all your land. They will besiege you in all your gates throughout all your land which Yahweh your God has given you.

Now therefore give me this hill country, of which Yahweh spoke in that day; for you heard in that day how the Anakim were there, and great and fortified cities. It may be that Yahweh will be with me, and I shall drive them out, as Yahweh said.”
They went out into the field, harvested their vineyards, trod the grapes, celebrated, and went into the house of their god and ate and drank, and cursed Abimelech.

David said to Abishai, “Now Sheba the son of Bichri will do us more harm than Absalom did. Take your lord’s servants, and pursue after him, lest he get himself fortified cities, and escape out of our sight.”
Now in the fourteenth year of king Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against all the fortified cities of Judah, and took them.
Haven’t you heard how I have done it long ago, and formed it of ancient times? Now I have brought it to pass, that it should be yours to lay waste fortified cities into ruinous heaps.
He placed forces in all the fortified cities of Judah, and set garrisons in the land of Judah, and in the cities of Ephraim, which Asa his father had taken.
He set judges in the land throughout all the fortified cities of Judah, city by city,
After these things and this faithfulness, Sennacherib king of Assyria came, entered into Judah, and encamped against the fortified cities, and intended to win them for himself.

Now after this, he built an outer wall to David’s city, on the west side of Gihon, in the valley, even to the entrance at the fish gate. He encircled Ophel with it, and raised it up to a very great height; and he put valiant captains in all the fortified cities of Judah.

They took fortified cities and a rich land, and possessed houses full of all good things, cisterns dug out, vineyards, olive groves, and fruit trees in abundance. So they ate, were filled, became fat, and delighted themselves in your great goodness.

definitions.short: to gather grapes ; also to be isolated (i.e. inaccessible by height or fortification)
definitions.usage: cut off, (de-) fenced, fortify, (grape) gather(-er), mighty things, restrain, strong, wall (up), withhold.
definitions.full: H1219. batsar [ בָּצַר ] verb cut off, make inaccessible (especially by fortifying), enclose (Late Hebrew id. , Aramaic בְּצַר , (Pa`el diminish, substract ), perhaps compare Arabic side, edge , , etc., rough stone , land in which are sharp stones (compare Lane)) — Qal Imperfect יִבְצֹר Psalm 76:13; 2 masculine singular תִּבְצֹר Lev 25:5 ; Deut 24:21 , וַיִּבְצְרוּ Judg 9:27 , תִּבְצְרוּ Lev 25:11 ; Participle active בּוֺצֵר Jer 6:9 , בֹּצְרִים 49:9 ; Obadiah 5; passive masculine בָּצוּר Zech 11:2 Kt (Qr בָּצִיר ), feminine בְּצוּרָה Isa 2:15 3 t. + Ezek 21:25 see below; plural feminine בְּצוּרוֺת 36:35 , בְּצֻרוֺת Num 13:28 14 t., בְּצוּרֹת Deut 1:28 ; Neh 9:25 , בְּצֻרֹת Deut 3:5 ; 9:1 ; — cut off , grape-clusters, ענבים Lev 25:5 , compare 25:11 (object נזיר ), Deut 24:21 ; Judg 9:27 (object in both, כרם ); hence Participle active grape-gathering, -gatherer Jer 6:9 ; 49:9 ; Obadiah 5; figurative cut off (= take away) Psalm 76:13 (object נגידים רות ); most often Passive participle cut off, made inaccessible , De Isa 2:15 = fortified , always f.; Generally adjective with ערים עיר, ; Num 13:28 ; Deut 1:28 ; 3:5 ; 9:1 ; Josh 14:12 ; 2Sam 20:6 ; 2Kin 18:13 = Isa 36:1 ; 2Kin 19:25 = Isa 37:26 ; 2Chr 17:2 ; 19:5 ; 32:1 ; 33:14 ; Neh 9:25 ; Isa 25:2 ; 27:10 ; Ezek 36:35 ; Hosea 8:14 ; Zeph 1:16 ; rarely with חומה Deut 28:52 ; Isa 2:15 ; Jer 15:20 ; הב ׳יער Zech 11:2 (read Kt); once, substantive of secrets, mysteries (= unattainable things) Jer 33:3 ; — ׳ב Ezek 21:25 ᵐ5 Sm Co בְּתוֺכָהּ , doubtless right. Niph`al Imperfect יִבָּצֵר be withheld Gen 11:6 ( מֵהֶם ), Job 42:2 ( מִמְּךָ ). Pi`el Imperfect 3feminine singular תְּבַצֵּר Jer 51:53 fortify ; so Infinitive לְבַּצֵר Isa 22:10 .
definitions.rootNote: a primitive root; to clip off; specifically (as denominative from 1210 )
